presentingComplaint: 3 days of worsening breathlessness and productive cough, referred as a query heart-failure decompensation.
history: Retired schoolteacher with HFrEF (EF 38%, on bisoprolol, ramipril, furosemide) and mild COPD (ex-smoker, 30 pack-years, no home oxygen). Over 3 days he developed a productive cough with yellow-green sputum, low-grade then higher fever, and a sharp right-sided chest pain worse on deep inspiration. Breathlessness increased from his baseline of climbing one flight to breathlessness on flat ground; he also noticed mild ankle swelling. His GP increased furosemide with little benefit and referred him as decompensated heart failure. No orthopnoea or PND beyond his chronic two-pillow baseline, no chest tightness on exertion, no haemoptysis, no calf pain or long-haul travel. No recent hospitalisation or antibiotics in the last 90 days. Adherent to cardiac medications.
examination: Alert and oriented, mildly dyspnoeic at rest but able to speak in full sentences. Warm peripheries. JVP not raised. Chest: bronchial breathing and coarse crepitations localised to the right lower zone with increased vocal resonance; scattered expiratory wheeze bilaterally at baseline; no bibasal fine crackles of pulmonary oedema. Heart sounds normal, no gallop, no new murmur. Mild bilateral pitting ankle oedema (chronic). Abdomen soft. No calf swelling or tenderness.

labs.ntprobnp: 890 pg/mL (near patient baseline, not markedly elevated)

imaging: Chest X-ray: dense right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms; no cardiomegaly change from prior film, no Kerley B lines, no upper-lobe diversion or pleural effusion suggesting fluid overload. Bedside lung ultrasound: focal B-lines with hepatisation and dynamic air bronchograms in the right base, not the bilateral diffuse B-line pattern of cardiogenic oedema.
microbiology: Sputum Gram stain: numerous polymorphs with Gram-positive diplococci. Blood cultures sent, pending. Pneumococcal urinary antigen positive. Nasopharyngeal respiratory viral panel negative.
differentialDiagnoses: Acute decompensated heart failure / cardiogenic pulmonary oedema (referral diagnosis; excluded by focal consolidation, only baseline NT-proBNP, absence of raised JVP/bibasal fine crackles)
Infective COPD exacerbation (wheeze present but focal lobar consolidation and pneumococcal antigen point to pneumonia)
Pulmonary embolism (pleuritic pain, but no tachycardia out of proportion, normal-ish oxygenation with clear consolidation explaining hypoxia)
Lung malignancy with post-obstructive pneumonia (age/smoking; requires interval CXR after treatment)
finalDiagnosis: Non-severe community-acquired pneumonia (right lower lobe, pneumococcal), CURB-65 = 1, in a patient with background HFrEF and COPD that mimicked heart-failure decompensation.
citations: ATS/IDSA - Diagnosis and Treatment of Adults with Community-Acquired Pneumonia - 2019
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e - Pneumonia
ICMR - Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (Community-Acquired Pneumonia) - 2019
stewardship: Non-severe CAP with cardiopulmonary comorbidity, treatable on the ward/oral route. Guideline-concordant empiric therapy targets S. pneumoniae plus atypical cover: amoxicillin-clavulanate plus a macrolide (or doxycycline). De-escalate to targeted therapy once pneumococcal antigen/culture confirmed; total 5 days if afebrile and clinically stable at 48-72h. Send blood cultures before antibiotics; do NOT escalate diuresis as primary therapy.
contraindications: Beta-lactam anaphylaxis (use respiratory fluoroquinolone or doxycycline + macrolide alternative)
Macrolide caution with QT-prolonging cardiac drugs / significant hepatic impairment
Avoid unnecessary furosemide up-titration - no objective evidence of fluid overload
edgeCases: NT-proBNP can be mildly raised in sepsis/pneumonia without heart failure - interpret against the patient's own baseline
Coexisting COPD wheeze can obscure focal consolidation - localised bronchial breathing is the key discriminator
In a smoker >50, a non-resolving opacity mandates a follow-up CXR at 6 weeks to exclude underlying malignancy
expectedMaiK: Non-severe community-acquired pneumonia (CURB-65 1); focal lobar consolidation with fever and purulent sputum distinguishes it from the referring heart-failure diagnosis.
expectedNextQuestions: Is the breathlessness accompanied by fever and purulent sputum rather than pure orthopnoea/PND?
Is there any recent hospitalisation or antibiotic exposure in the last 90 days (HAP/MDR risk)?
What is the patient's baseline exercise tolerance and NT-proBNP for comparison?
Any smoking history or prior abnormal chest imaging warranting malignancy follow-up?
expectedInvestigations: SpO2 / arterial blood gas if hypoxic
regressionAssertions: Engine must return CAP as the top diagnosis despite the heart-failure referral framing.
heart_failure must appear only as a differential, not the final diagnosis, given focal consolidation and non-elevated NT-proBNP relative to baseline.
Severity must be classified as non-severe (CURB-65 = 1); must NOT trigger SEVERE_CAP.
Empiric recommendation must include a beta-lactam (amoxicillin-clavulanate) plus atypical cover (macrolide/doxycycline), not diuretic escalation.
Recommended duration should be 5 days with clinical stability review at 48-72h.
